notes.title: Devlog 5 - "The Last 10%"
notes.content:
[p]Things have taken a bit longer than expected. More specifically, there's a lot more [i]stuff[/i] to do than I expected. It's very easy, as a developer, to just "ignore" the areas of the game that need polish. As I started playtesting more thoroughly, those problem spots became a lot more clear. There aren't [i]that[/i] many major issues, but there's a [i]lot[/i] of minor ones. [/p][p]
In combination with those issues, I underestimated the amount of UI and animation work that needed to be done. The game still [i]barely[/i] has any sound effects! As such, I don't have much choice but to push the demo back.[/p][p][/p][p]I'm not sure how [i]long[/i] that delay will be, but I wouldn't expect it to release in October. I'd be [i]surprised[/i] to see it reach into December, but it's possible - I once thought it was going to release in August (how silly that seems now). [/p][p][/p][p]To summarize what remains:[/p][list][*][p][b]Battle Content[/b] - Almost entirely complete. Minor balancing, and external testing, are all that remains.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Battle UI[/b] - Everything is [i]implemented[/i], but there's 3 places which need some reworking and new assets. I don't expect this to be more than ~2 days of combined work, once I properly sit down for it.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Battle Visuals/Sound[/b] - Needs a lot of stuff. There's about 1/8th of the necessary animations in the game right now, and like 1/30th of the needed SFX. None of these are [i]hard[/i] to do, but they [i]are[/i] time consuming. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Dialogue[/b] - All scripts are written, but still need to be transcribed into Yarnscript and given stage directions. Another ~2 day task, considering the code-side stuff that still needs to be done. Need to make some final UI assets as well, but that's less [i]necessary[/i].[/p][/*][*][p][b]Teambuilder[/b] - Very close to done. I've reworked the UI for this to a state I'm quite happy about. With 1-2 minor tweaks, it's as finished as it can get.[/p][/*][*][p][b]"Stage Select" [/b]- Mostly done, still needs me to finish off some UI assets. Functionality is almost all in.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Tutorial [/b]- 30-40% done. Most tutorials are written, but implementing them is a pain with my systems. Definitely the thing I've been procrastinating the most.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Core Polish [/b]- This category doesn't really make sense outside of my own task list, but consists of things that [i]must[/i] be in the game and aren't tied to any specific system. For example, a Settings page and a scene transition effect.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Art Assets [/b]- 2-3 assets away from having everything in. Still need one dialogue sprite, one combat sprite, and a "generic person" dialogue sprite.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Music[/b] - Done? Depends on if I get more perfectionist about it.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]That's a lot of stuff. I'm going to try and update this each week (or at [i]least[/i] every other week) with progress. In the meantime, here's a screenshot of the (WIP) new teambuilder/overworld UI:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45671074/4d00145c47faea194848c2ee35152d9d64fe0c5a.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Devlog #4: Closing in on Demo
notes.content:
[p]Howdy! [/p][p][/p][p]It's been a minute since I last posted one of these. I've been waiting until I hit a major milestone, and am glad to say that I have! The demo is now [i]content complete[/i]. Every enemy, ability, and mechanic has been implemented! Some of it will most likely change as I start playtesting, but they're all here now. Unfortunately, this [i]does not[/i] mean the Demo is right around the corner - though it is getting close.[/p][p][/p][p]Now that all the content is implemented, theres four major goals remaining:[/p][list][*][p]Implement final animations[/p][/*][*][p]Fix the ugly UI (and get all final art assets)[/p][/*][*][p]Playtest, Playtest, Playtest[/p][/*][*][p]Polish, Polish, Polish[/p][/*][/list][p]In order to launch a Demo, I 'need' to make a trailer. In order to make a good trailer, I need much better looking visuals. Thankfully, I have most of what I need to make that happen. It's just going to take a good chunk of time.[/p][p]Once a trailer is out, I'm planning to reach out to smaller content creators in order to get some eyes on the demo. Once that process is done, the demo will release. I'd expect it to take 1-2 weeks after the trailer as I market and polish it.[/p][p]My original goal was to complete the demo in September. I think this is still [i]roughly[/i] in the cards, but the demo won't [i]release[/i] until October (hopefully fairly early). [/p][p]I'll be trying to release these updates weekly until it drops (though they were supposed to be weekly in the first place, so who knows). [/p][p][/p][p]In the meantime, here's a sprite preview for the new Dancer boss![/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45671074/763f2b8011b86284519ceedbecc74df32cd8c9fc.png"][/img]
[/p]

notes.title: Devlog 3 - Raid Mechanics in a TRPG
notes.content:
[p]Howdy!
Last log I promised info on the Sparks (classes) system, but I'm hoping to finish up some UI related to that first. Instead, I'm going to give a bit more of a "design breakdown" here - how I'm implementing FFXIV-esque raid mechanics into a TRPG. First, heres a quick update on everything done since the last post:[/p][list][*][p]The new boss has been ~60% implemented, and almost all "new" code for it has been written. Pending a major bugfix, the first phase is functionally done.[/p][/*][*][p]The map has been heavily updated, and is nearly in a final state codewise. Just need to implement a few extra details into node transitions, and link scenes together (so that a Dialogue scene can go directly into a Battle scene, for example).[/p][/*][*][p]Some major performance optimizations, implemented after I realized there were some critical problems with it. This is why I'm behind on a few other things, and I'm not confident its 100% done.[/p][/*][*][p]First-draft scripts for all dialogue scenes in the demo. Still missing some other dialogue - combat barks and map narration primarily - but its getting closer.[/p][/*][*][p]Dialogue art for another character, and the second-phase sprite for the new boss[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Now, regarding design:[/p][p][/p][p]One of my main goals when starting this project was to make "good" tactics game bosses. I've played a decent few TRPG's now and the bosses were almost always the lowpoints of the game, usually underwhelming [i]at best[/i]. As I was in the early stages, i was also playing through the previous FFXIV raid tier and absolutely loving it. The "coordinated dance" feel, the way your rotation mixes with the bosses movements, the static positions for different mechanics - I realized you could probably transpose it into a grid based format.[/p][p][/p][p]Around this same time, I was getting into the works of Project Moon. The way their bosses are designed, as puzzles to be solved rather than bags of purely HP, felt like it would fit very smoothly into that "dancelike" format. And thus, I began to finalize the design ideas for Fractal Odyssey bosses.[/p][p][/p][p]Along these lines, I've conceptualized every boss as two major components: the "puzzle" and the "dance". [/p][p]The Puzzle is the first part of the fight, where the player is learning what the enemy actually [i]does[/i]. More importantly, its where the player figures out how to counter the boss mechanics - how to take advantage of the openings the enemy gives.[/p][p]The Dance only begins once the Puzzle has been solved, and it is the act of countering the mechanics itself. Dodging standard attacks, baiting the enemy into bad positions, figuring out how to keep as many units in range as possible - it is a constant series of smaller puzzles to solve each turn. This should grow in complexity as the fight continues, aiming to always end on a crescendo.[/p][p][/p][p]To give an example from the first phase of the new boss (note that this is all subject to change):[/p][list][*][p]It inflicts a debuff called "Flame" onto one of your units. This causes it, several turns later, to attack all of the tiles in an X shape from that unit.[/p][/*][*][p]It inflicts a debuff called "Waltz" onto one of your units. This debuff is transferred to another unit when the debuff expires, only if that other unit is adjacent to the holder. After someone loses Waltz, they gain "Flame" (and keep regaining it). This creates an increasingly large area of denial, entirely based on your own positioning.[/p][/*][*][p]The boss will attack with small, delayed, AOE attacks regularly. This forces your units to constantly move, and prevents a single "solved" positioning from being found.[/p][/*][*][p]The boss will regularly move, and use line attacks of its own. This requires the player to either keep repositioning to safely hit it with their damage dealers, or rely on weaker (and safer!) ranged options.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p]From my personal (and obviously biased) playtesting, this sort of design has created a very fun battle loop during these fights. There's always several factors to consider at once, proactive defense tools to allow for mistakes, and the ticking clock of the games low-healing nature.[/p][p][/p][p]If you read this, and are interested in playtesting this prior to the demo release, feel free to join the [url="https://discord.gg/beDPyB2Qfr"]Discord[/url]. I'll be putting out a playtester call, probably in a month or so. 
To whoever reads this, thank you for your time! I hope you found this interesting.[/p]

notes.title: Devlog 2 - Tutorials, Animations, Progression
notes.content:
[p]Howdy!
[/p][p]Here's an update on how things have been going:[/p][p][/p][p][b]Tutorials[/b] [/p][list][*][p]The core systems for the Tutorial have been implemented, as well as the very initial tutorials themselves. At this point, all that needs to be added here is the "content" - all of the text, the special tutorial rules, the tutorial stages themselves, etc.[/p][/*][*][p]This is in a "chip away at it over time" state, since actually solely working on tutorials is painfully mind-numbing. [/p][/*][*][p]There's rough plans for a "see tutorials you've already viewed" system, though that might not make the cut for the demo.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]Animations[/b][/p][list][*][p]After a lot of experimenting, I've finally found a reasonable and cost-efficient way to get animations made quickly and in large quantities.[/p][/*][*][p]Basically, I'm taking the pixelart animations made by [url="https://frostwindz.itch.io"]Frostwindz[/url] and (with permission from the original creator) tracing them into a hand-drawn style to match the games aesthetic. This obviously won't be perfect, but it lets my minimal art skill contribute.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]Progression[/b][/p][list][*][p]I've been travelling a lot recently, which kinda prohibited me from doing much proper code work. Instead, I've been able to get a lot of design work done. Character customization, levelling, and general game structure are approaching a "final" form for both the full game and the demo. Mostly numbers to tweak on that stuff now.[/p][/*][*][p]I've also been reworking most of the player unit kits and equippable Sparks (classes) to feel a bit beefier to use. I'll hopefully spotlight these, alongside the combat system at large, in the next post.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Over the next week or so, I'm going to be working on finalizing the Map (level select) screen, and fully implementing saving. Pretty confident at this point the demo won't be coming until September, but also pretty confident it won't be later. I'm sure I'll eat those words.[/p][p][/p][p]In the meantime, here's a little art teaser:

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45671074/5e45607816ae9f23861390d3649bf136dd7e425a.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Devlog 1 - What we're working on!
notes.content:
[p]Howdy!
First off, I'd like to thank everyone who's been following the project so far, and everyone who's wishlisted - it means a lot!
I'm "Mega" - lead developer. I do basically everything aside from the visual art, and originally started this project completely solo. Honestly, I never expected it to get this far - having a steam page feels unreal even a week later.

I'll be doing these devlogs every 1-2 weeks to share progress as we approach the end of the summer and, hopefully, our demo release. This log will be more of an overview of what we have left to do.[/p][p][/p][p]I have four main goals in mind, things that [i]must[/i] be done before I'd consider the demo "good enough":[/p][list][*][p]A full-featured tutorial. This is my current target, and probably the most important thing here. The main point of feedback in previous playtests was the the mechanics were unclear, and the game felt overly knowledge-demanding. This is getting close-ish to done, and I'll probably be running a "tutorial playtest" soon. Join the [url="https://discord.gg/beDPyB2Qfr"]Discord [/url]if you're interested, I'll be sharing it through there. Full details on this will be in the next devlog (probably).[/p][/*][*][p]Complete dialogue scenes (and overall Chapter 1 story). Most of the systems for dialogue are in place, I have a functioning prototype set up, but we still need to finish a lot of visual art and writing. [/p][/*][*][p]Midgame boss. Since the demo will consist of Chapter 1 only, I want to include some later-game content to give a sense of "where things will go" with the mechanics. This fight has a more-or-less completed design, has art in progress, and hasn't started implementation yet. I think it should make some of my inspirations, especially FFXIV raid design, much more clear. [/p][/*][*][p]Polish, Polish, Polish. Battle has lots of rough visual edges - animations are sparse and lack impact, sound is barely implemented, post-processing is completely untouched, etc. This is an ongoing process rather than a discrete step, but that means progress is always being made. I think I've found a good process for animations and icons, so thats the next immediate step.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]I don't have anything this week, but hopefully going forward I'll include an art or music teaser alongside these posts. Thanks for reading, and please Wishlist if you haven't already![/p]
